topicName: Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Clusters, Pods, Deployments, Services
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Clusters, Pods, Deployments, Services"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) provides a managed environment for deploying, managing, and scaling your containerized applications using Google infrastructure. This tutorial covers the core concepts of GKE: Clusters, Pods, Deployments, and Services."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Kubernetes Clusters"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Kubernetes cluster represents the foundation of your GKE environment. It consists of a control plane (master node) and worker nodes. The control plane manages the cluster, while the worker nodes run your applications."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Control Plane: Manages the cluster state, scheduling, and API access."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Worker Nodes: Virtual machines (VMs) that run your containerized applications. Each node is part of the cluster and managed by the control plane."},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create a GKE cluster using the Google Cloud Console or the `gcloud` command-line tool."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"gcloud container clusters create my-cluster --zone us-central1-a --num-nodes 3"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command creates a cluster named 'my-cluster' in the 'us-central1-a' zone with 3 worker nodes."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Pods"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes. It represents a single instance of a running process in your cluster. A Pod can contain one or more containers that share network and storage resources."},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's an example Pod definition in YAML:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: my-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: my-container
    image: nginx:latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"This Pod definition specifies a single container running the 'nginx:latest' image and exposing port 80."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Deployments"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deployments manage the desired state of your application. They ensure that a specified number of Pod replicas are running at all times. Deployments also handle updates and rollbacks to your application."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's an example Deployment definition in YAML:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: my-container
        image: nginx:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"This Deployment definition specifies 3 replicas of the Pod defined in the 'template' section. It uses a 'selector' to identify the Pods managed by the Deployment."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"To apply this deployment, use the following command:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Services"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Service provides a stable IP address and DNS name for accessing your application. It acts as a load balancer, distributing traffic across the Pods managed by a Deployment."},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's an example Service definition in YAML:"},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: my-app
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 80
  type: LoadBalancer"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"This Service definition selects Pods with the label 'app: my-app' and exposes them on port 80. The 'type: LoadBalancer' setting provisions a Google Cloud Load Balancer to distribute traffic to the Pods."},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"To apply this service, use the following command:"},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"kubectl apply -f service.yaml"},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"After applying the service, you can retrieve the external IP address of the load balancer using the following command:"},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":"kubectl get service my-service"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic overview of GKE Clusters, Pods, Deployments, and Services. These components are fundamental to deploying and managing containerized applications on Google Cloud. Further exploration of topics like autoscaling, networking, and storage is recommended for advanced use cases."}]
